1  ORAL ORDER (PER : HONOURABLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MRS. JUSTICE SUNITA AGARWAL)
1. No one has put in appearance on behalf of the petitioners.
2. The present petition was taken up on 21.9.2023 when after going through the record of the writ petition, this Court has noted that the petitioners who claim to be the purchasers of the land in question by way of three registered sale deeds NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/13765/2018 ORDER DATED: 30/09/2024 undefined dated 22.7.2008, 3.6.2009 and 6.8.2009 through the power of attorney holder of respondent No.10 (now deceased) claim right to receive compensation.

Initially suit namely Special Civil Suit No. 556 of 2010 was filed by the deceased respondent No.10 before the Principal Senior Civil Judge, Ahmedabad (R) seeking cancellation of the sale deeds and other two suits namely Special Civil Suit No. 392 of 2012 and Special Civil Suit No. 397 of 2012 were filed by the petitioners.
However, all the three suits had been dismissed as withdrawn on an alleged compromise arrived between the parties, reference of which has been made in Para-3 of the writ petition.
It was noted in the order dated 21.9.2023 that the correct and complete facts have not been brought on record.
Neither the sale deed nor the plaint of the Civil Suits filed by the parties or the orders passed by the Civil Court are on record.
In absence of these documents, no adjudication can be made.
It was also noted that there is no categorical response in the affidavit filed by respondent No.10.

At that stage, both the learned advocates appearing for the parties sought adjournments to enable them to file affidavits to bring on record correct and complete facts with respect to the names of the petitioners.
Inspite of the categorical orders passed by us, over a period of one year, no affidavit has been filed by any of the parties.
Be that as it may, we proceed to decide the matter on the basis of the material on record.

2. Further, from the record of the writ petition, it may be noted that the writ petition has been filed with the following prayers:
NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/13765/2018 ORDER DATED: 30/09/2024 undefined "17.

In view of the facts stated herein above, the petitioners most respectfully pray that:-
(A) YOUR LORDSHIPS may be pleased to admit and allow this petition.
(B) YOUR LORDSHIPS may be pleased to issue a writ of certiorari or any other appropriate writ, order of direction, quashing and setting aside Order dated 23.08.2018, 30.08.2018 passed by special Land acquisition Officer Under Section 11 of the Act and under application filled by petitioners to make reference under section 18 of the said Act.
(C) YOUR LORDSHIPS may be pleased to issue a writ of Mendamus or any other appropriate writ,
order of direction, Directing Special land Acquisition officer to refer dispute to the Civil Court in accordance with Section 18 or 30 or 31 of the Act.

, YOUR LORDSHIP may be pleased to stay implementation, operation and execution of the order dated 23.08.2018 and subsequant order passed on the date of 30.08.2018 by special Land Acquisition officer Under Section 11 of the Act."

3. The challenge in the writ petition is to the award dated 23.8.2018 passed under Section 11 of the Land Acquisition Act and the order of rejection of the application under Section NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/13765/2018 ORDER DATED: 30/09/2024 undefined 18 filed by the petitioners for making reference.

From the facts stated in the writ petition, it may be noted that it is an admitted facts that the land in question is a land of ownership of the deceased respondent No.10,
who stated to have executed three sale deeds in favour of the petitioners dated 22.7.2008, 11.9.2009 and 6.9.2009 for Survey Nos. 209, 379, 371 through three different Power of attorneys and that sale consideration had been received.
It seems that the original owner namely respondent No.10 had disputed the transactions and instituted Special Civil Suit No. 556 of 2010 before the Principal Senior Civil Judge, Ahmedabad (Rural).
Simultaneously, the petitioners had filed Civil Suit No. 312 of 2012 and Civil Suit No. 397 of 2012.
4. It is stated that respondent No.10 compelled the petitioners to enter into settlement on a promise to pay the sum decided into settlement deed executed on 17.7.2012.

Both the petitioners and respondent No.10 had withdrawn the Suits against each other and it was decided that respondent No.10 would receive Rs.2,16,00,000/- out of the amount of compensation, which is Rs.9,02,05,200/-, and the rest of the amount would be paid to the petitioners.

5. However, respondent No.10 did not honour the settlement deed and hence the petitioners filed three civil suits, Civil Suit No.182 (574/2013), 183 (575/2013) and 184 (576/2013) of 2017, for declaration of ownership, injunction against respondent No.10 and for specific performance of NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/13765/2018 ORDER DATED: 30/09/2024 undefined settlement deed.

During the pendency of the said Suits before the Civil Court, respondent No.10 filed an affidavit before the reference Court in LAR No. 75 of 2013 stating that there were no litigation pending before any Court and the parties had come to a settlement and received Rs.28,87,318/- out of the total award of the acquisition.

6. As the respondent No.10 had received compensation by making a false statement, the petitioner filed Special Civil Suit No. 6791 of 2017 which was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to file Suit for Recovery of the said amount from respondent No.10.
Resultantly, the petitioners filed Special Civil Suit No. 73/2018 before the Civil Judge Senior Division, Sanand, which is still pending.

7. From the statement made in Para-3 of the writ petition, it may be noted that the petitioners have not appended the copy of the plaint of any of the Civil Suits or the order passed by the competent Court of withdrawal of the suits filed by the petitioners and respondent No.10 or the plaint of the Civil Suit pending as on the date of filing of the writ petition.

8. Be that as it may, it is further stated that as per the contention in the writ petition, the successor-in-interest of respondent No.10 had filed Civil Suit Nos. 92/2011, 189/2011 and 479/2012 Mansukhbhai Ramanbhai vs State Of Gujarat Through Concerned App on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37062644/
3 before the Civil Court, Ahmedabad (Rural), which came to be withdrawn by respondent Nos. 5, 6 ,7 and 8, claiming to be successor- in-interest of respondent No.10.

sentences.text: The copy of the order of withdrawal of the said suit is also not on NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/13765/2018 ORDER DATED: 30/09/2024 undefined record.

Other statements made in the writ petition about the revision appeal filed and the Regular Civil Appeal No.221 of 2012 filed and withdrawn by respondent Nos.11 and 12 are also not supported by any material on record.

9. It is further contended that respondent Nos.5, 6, 7 and 8 initiated Regular Civil Suit No. 325 of 2016 before the Civil Court, Ahmedabad (Rural) against the respondent No.10 for restraining the respondent No.10 from receiving the amount under the award as also for restraining respondent Nos.2 and 3 from initiating payment of the award to respondent No.3.
The said suit was filed on the basis of the Memorandum of Understanding executed between respondent Nos. 5 to 9 and respondent No.10, on 20.4.2013.

The copy of the order passed by the Senior Civil Judge,
Ahmedabad (Rural) dated 11.5.2017 in the said suit has been attached as Annexure "A" to the writ petition.
Further, there is a narration of the challenge made by respondent Nos. 5 to 9 to the orders passed in the suits filed by them.

10. It is further contended that the petitioner has filed an application under Order 1 Rule 10 CPC for impleadment in Regular Civil Suit No. 325 of 2016 filed by the respondent Nos. 5, 6, 7 and 8 before the Civil Court, Ahmedabad (Rural).
The said application was dismissed by order dated 14.12.2016 against which the Civil Revision No. 79 of 2016 was filed by the petitioner which is still pending before this Court.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/13765/2018 ORDER DATED: 30/09/2024 undefined 11.

With these averments made in the writ petition, it is submitted that the respondent No.2 namely Special Land Acquisition Officer has passed an order dated 23.8.2018 holding that respondent No.10 was the owner of the land in question and the remaining amount under the award not being under Section 30/31 of the Land Acquisition Act, the prayer made for the said amount to be deposited before the Civil Court has been rejected.
12. On the receipt of the order dated 23.8.2018, a consent deed had been executed between the GIDC and respondent No.10 that the remaining amount of award shall be paid to respondent No.10.

As soon as the order dated 23.8.2018 passed by the respondent No.2 was received by the petitioners,
the petitioners immediately made an application to respondent No.2 to make a reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act as the order dated 23.8.2018 was passed under Section 11(2)
of the said Act.

The application for making reference filed by the petitioners has been rejected and hence this writ petition.
13.

From the facts stated in the writ petition, it is more than evident that the question as to whether the petitioners would be entitled to receive compensation or the award of the compensation to respondent No.10 is bad, is to be decided in the pending Civil Suit filed by the petitioners,
admittedly, for declaration of ownership for injunction against respondent No.10 and for specific performance of settlement deed.

sentences.text: NEUTRAL
CITATION
ORDER DATED: 30/09/2024 undefined him namely Special Civil Suit No. 73 of 2018 is also stated to be pending before the competent Court.
14. As far as orders passed by respondent No.2 are concerned, they are consent awards under Section 11(2) and the application for making reference filed under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act.

The question as to whether the petitioners would be entitled to make a reference and would inherit right or would acquire right in the property in question on the basis of the sale deed, is a question to be decided by the Civil Court.

15. It may further be noted from the order-sheet of this case that after the interim order was passed by this Court on 7.9.2018, there are repeated adjournments in the matter and the interim order has been extended from time to time from the year 2018 onwards.
On none of the date fixed, the matter was argued by the learned advocates for the parties.

Even after the last order dated 21.9.2023 wherein direction was given to the parties to file affidavit to bring on record the correct and complete facts with regard to claim of the petitioners, nothing has been brought on record.
16. We, therefore, do not find any good ground to keep the writ petition pending.

The present writ petition is being disposed of in the absence of the learned advocate for the petitioner, with the observation that the issues raised in the writ petition may be agitated before the Competent Civil Court in the pending Civil Suits, which have to be decided NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/13765/2018 ORDER DATED: 30/09/2024 undefined strictly in accordance with law without being influenced by any of the observations made hereinabove.
The connected Civil Application also stands disposed of, accordingly.
